newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Five E. European states set for EU talks.
newsitem.headline: Five E. European states set for EU talks.

text.p: The European Commission plans to recommend opening membership talks with five eastern European countries and Cyprus next week, EU officials said on Monday.

"The assessment that the (EU Commission) services have made to date would suggest that they would recommend on the basis of objective criteria to start negotiations with six," one official, who declined to be named, told Reuters.

Another official told Reuters that Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic -- widely seen as the frontrunners -- would be named in a first wave of talks when the EU executive gives its opinion on July 16 on how ready 10 eastern countries' are for membership.
An initial draft under consideration by the 20 Commissioners also points to Estonia and Slovenia as being ready, he said.
Cyprus, which has already been deemed suitable for EU membership and has been waiting for some time to be called for talks, is being pushed heavily by Greece.
Slovakia, Latvia, Lithuania, Bulgaria and Romania have also applied for membership.

Some of the more advanced applicants had feared that failure by EU leaders to agree at their June 16-17 summit in Amsterdam on instsitutional changes needed to adapt the EU to the needs of more members would limit the EU's next enlargement wave to five countries.
The nordic countries and their European Commissioners have been strongly pushing the case of Estonia, while the southern Commissioners have been pushing Slovenia.
The easterners at the back of the queue had been pushing for talks with all 10 to take place at the same time.

Many of them face a double rejection as the NATO military alliance is expected to invite only Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary to a first round of enlargement talks when its leaders meet in Madrid on Tuesday and Wednesday.
